name: Automated freeze substitution of high-pressure-frozen samples in a Leica AFS2: -90 °C hold, 5 °C/h to -20 °C, 10 °C/h to 20 °C
plain_name: Slowly swap ice for solvent in frozen cells before embedding them in resin
description: High-pressure-frozen specimens on 6 mm sapphire disks are transferred into cryotubes of fixative in acetone at -90 °C and warmed under program control (-90 °C for 5-30 h, 5 °C/h to -20 °C, 12 h at -20 °C, 10 °C/h to 20 °C) so that ice is replaced by solvent before resin embedding for electron microscopy.
keywords: Slowly swap ice for solvent in frozen cells before embedding them in resin

sources.citation: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

Rachid R, Wendt C, de Souza W, Miranda K (2026). Optimisation of freeze substitution protocols for the examination of malaria parasite structure by volumetric electron microscopy. Journal of Microscopy. doi:10.1111/jmi.70007

requirements.rationale: The programme spans -90 °C (183.15 K) to 20 °C (293.15 K).
Independent protocol: chamber pre-cooled to -90 °C before samples enter the freeze-substitution medium.
The 6 mm middle plate / sapphire disk is released into acetone pre-cooled in the AFS chamber.
The fastest programmed warming step is 10 °C/h (166.67 mK/min, rounded up to 167); the unit must ramp at least this fast under control.
Frozen specimens and the osmium/glutaraldehyde fixative tubes are kept and transferred under liquid nitrogen.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
